text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday.
- Serbs in Vukovar attack Croatian journalists reporting on an exhibition of paintings by Serb and Croat children.
- The government's office for transitional administration moving from Osijek to Borovo and Beli Manastir on Monday.
- Central bank: Currency reserves suffice to preserve stability.
- Economy Minister Davor Stern begins a visit to Indonesia.
- New modes of social welfare assistance to be introduced in February: Social welfare payouts to go up, but the number of people receiving them to be cut.
- After Croatia Airlines decided to buy new planes from Airbus, talks are now to follow on a deadline for delivery of the first A-319. Foreign banks expected to finance the $45 million dollar deal.
- The dream of all ethnic Albanians is for Kosovo to become independent, says Azem Vllasi, former Albanian political leader, in an interview.

- Interview with UNHCR's spokesperson, Alemka Lisinski: The mass return of Bosnian refugees to their homes is still a long way away and will happen only when all sides allow it. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
